what_this_is: Soft-magnetic material constants and real core geometries, transcribed from the vendor pages named in every row's `source`. This is NOT a design rule: every number here is one vendor's published typical value at one condition, and the condition is stored with it.
what_this_is_not: Not a Steinmetz fit FOR YOU. Every `steinmetz` field is null on purpose, because that slot holds a material-level si triple (k/alpha/beta) and no vendor publishes one in that shape. What the powder vendor DOES publish - a curve fit PL = a*Bpk^b*f^c per permeability, per core shape and, for the High DC Bias product lines, per variant, in mW/cm3 / T / kHz - is transcribed verbatim into `loss_fit` with its catalog page and its unit triple, and magnetics_material_core_loss evaluates it. Five powder materials carry one (Kool Mu, MPP, High Flux, XFlux, Edge); the ferrite vendors' own fits were still unreachable in a quotable form on 2026-11-01, so those materials refuse rather than guess.
Not a thermal model. No Rth (thermal resistance) was found for any part, so select_core reports watts and refuses a temperature rise.

Not a B-H curve. `bsat` is one point (or two, if the vendor published two temperatures); the shape between the points, the DC-bias roll-off of AL, and the temperature coefficient of AL are all missing.
Not every grade of every shape. The rows are the ones whose vendor page actually stated the numbers; absence is recorded as absence, not filled in.

unit_notes.al_nh: inductance factor, nH/turn^2, at the gap stated in `gap_um` (0 = ungapped). Vendor tolerance is in `al_tolerance_pct` where published.
unit_notes.amin_mm2: minimum cross-section (vendor 'Amin'), mm^2 - the flux density peak is bounded by THIS, not by Ae, in a core whose centre leg is narrower than the outer legs
unit_notes.mass_g: set mass (both halves for a two-piece core) unless `mass_basis` says otherwise
unit_notes.loss_ref: the ONE measured loss point the vendor published for this part, with its condition. f_khz is kilohertz - note that not every vendor measures at 100 kHz.
unit_notes.aw_mm2: usable winding area of the matching coil former, mm^2 (vendor 'winding area'). Only present where a former datasheet was reachable.
unit_notes.mlt_mm: mean length per turn for the matching coil former, mm (vendor 'average length of turn')

density_vs_permeability_60u.what_this_is: the catalog's approximate factor for turning the 60u density of a powder material into the density of the same material at another permeability. Printed p.16: 'The approximate densities of other permeabilities are related to 60u density by the factors shown'
density_vs_permeability_60u.note_on_the_gap: the table lists fourteen permeabilities (14 to 550) but prints factors for only eleven of them; 200u, 300u and 550u appear in the column with no factor beside them, so no factor is invented here - for those the vendor points at the individual data sheet

materials.name: Kool Mu
materials.mu_i_note: sold as discrete permeabilities 14 / 19 / 26 / 40 / 60 / 75 / 90 / 125 - there is no single mu_i
materials.bsat_note: vendor states 10500 G = 1.05 T for the material; it is a distributed-gap powder so this is the material's own saturation, not a DC-bias limit of a part
materials.tc_note: Curie temperature printed as 500 C (printed p.16, Material Properties) - typical, not a guaranteed minimum
materials.density_note: 5.8 g/cm3 at 60u, printed p.16. The same table prints density for the 60u permeability of every material and gives factors for the others (see density_vs_permeability_60u). Kool Mu MAX 6.5, H-f 6.0 and Ultra 6.0 are printed separately, so the variant rows must not inherit this number
materials.steinmetz_note: null on purpose: this slot holds a material-level si triple (k/alpha/beta) and the powder vendor does not publish one that way. Its actual curve fit - a, b, c per permeability and per core shape - is in `loss_fit` with its catalog page, and magnetics_material_core_loss evaluates it

loss_fit.b_is: peak flux density = HALF the ac swing; the catalog defines Bpk = (B_ac_max - B_ac_min)/2
loss_fit.varies_with: permeability AND core shape, not material alone - the catalog prints a separate fit for toroids, E/U/EER cores, EQ/LP cores and blocks
loss_fit.not_a_spec: a curve fit of the vendor's measured loss curves, not a guaranteed limit; the vendor's own charts are the authority
loss_fit.frequency_khz_below: the row applies only below this frequency - the catalog splits the Ultra fit at 100 kHz
loss_fit.frequency_khz_above: the row applies only above this frequency
